title: Holiday sales forecast for a small online shop with only two years of data
summary: Two holiday seasons of one fictional shop, and a forecast that is honest enough to be a range instead of a number.

blocks.title: Two data points is not a trend
blocks.body: A fictional candle-and-soap shop has two Novembers and two Decembers behind it, and has to decide how much stock to build for this holiday season. The honest forecast is a range with reasoning, not a number with confidence.

blocks.heading: What the two years actually say
blocks.caption: Fictional shop, fictional numbers - the shape (growth plus a holiday spike) is the real subject.

blocks.heading: Two things are growing at once
blocks.body: The baseline is drifting up about 10% a year - that is the shop growing. The holiday spike is also growing faster - November and December rose 18 to 24%. Are holiday sales a multiple of baseline (year one: December was 3.1x September; year two: 3.5x), or is the spike itself inflating? Two years cannot separate those stories. That is the entire problem.

columns.name: Floor: $24,500
columns.detail: The spike ratio stays at year one's 3.1x against a baseline that grew 10%. Assumes year two's stronger ratio was luck, weather, or one good post.

columns.name: Middle: $26,800
columns.detail: The ratio holds at year two's 3.5x. Assumes nothing got better or worse - the single least-crazy assumption available.

columns.name: Ceiling: $29,500
columns.detail: The ratio keeps climbing to 3.9x, continuing the two-year pattern. Possible, and indistinguishable from a story you are telling yourself.

items.label: Holiday seasons of data. That is why this is a range

blocks.heading: Stocking against a range instead of a number
items: Build to the floor plus the firm pre-orders you actually hold. That stock is safe.
Secure the ability to make more fast - materials on hand, a second pour weekend penciled in - sized to reach the middle.
Do not build to the ceiling. Unsold candles in January are the tuition for believing your own story.
Write down which scenario you stocked to and why. Next year there will be three data points, and the note is what makes the third one useful.

blocks.title: What would actually shrink the range
blocks.body: Not more spreadsheet. Pre-orders, email-list response rates, and week-by-week sell-through in November - leading indicators that arrive before the decision is locked. The third year of data helps most, and there is no shortcut to it.

blocks.heading: Check the instinct
blocks.prompt: Why not just forecast $26,800 and stock to it?
options: Because the point estimate hides the uncertainty; stocking and staffing decisions need the range, not the average
Because rounding to the nearest hundred is more accurate
blocks.explanation: With two years of data the true December plausibly sits anywhere in a $5,000 band. A single number pretends the band does not exist, and the build-or-hold decisions price very differently at the floor than at the ceiling.
